title: T Cell Immunity to Bacterial Pathogens: Mechanisms of Immune Control and Bacterial Evasion
summary: Review establishing the definitional basis of the TRDV2 marker used in the atlas label. Human gamma-delta T cells are divided by TCR delta-chain (TRDV gene) usage into TRDV1+ (Vδ1+) and TRDV2+ (Vδ2+) subsets; TRDV2 is a transcript/gene-segment marker of the Vδ2 lineage. TRDV2+ (Vδ2+) cells dominate peripheral blood and pair almost exclusively TRGV9 with TRDV2 to form innate-like, phosphoantigen-reactive Vγ9Vδ2 T cells. This anchors TRDV2 as a gamma-delta (not alpha-beta) lineage marker.
quotes: In humans, γδ T cells can be classified into two main populations, based on their expression of TCR δ-chains encoded by two TRDV genes-TRDV1 + γδ T cells (or Vδ1 + T cells) and TRDV2 + γδ T cells (or Vδ2 + T cells).
Vδ1 + T cells are abundant in the skin, intestine, and uterus, whereas Vδ2 + T cells constitute the majority of peripheral blood γδ T cells [24,173,174].

Vδ2 + T cells are dominated by TCR γδ chain rearrangements encoded by the TRGV9 and TRDV2 segments, which almost exclusively pair together, forming the more frequently termed "Vγ9 + Vδ2 +" T cells that make up large proportions of peripheral blood γδ T cells in humans and other species [175].

title: Gamma Delta T-lymphocytes in Hepatitis C and Chronic Liver Disease
summary: Review defining CD161/KLRB1 as a marker and its expression on gamma-delta T cells. CD161 (KLRB1) is a C-type lectin membrane glycoprotein expressed on NK cells, ~24% of peripheral T cells, and on both alpha-beta and gamma-delta T cells; here CD161 is discussed as a surface/protein marker (flow/immunostaining) while KLRB1 is its gene. CD161 marks a memory phenotype in the gamma-delta compartment and is associated with tissue-homing (gut/liver) and shared with MAIT cells — the shared CD161 expression is a key source of the MAIT/γδ transcriptional overlap seen in the atlas label.
quotes: CD161 [also known as killer lectin receptor subfamily B member 1 (KLRB1)] is a C-type lectin membrane glycoprotein that is expressed on the majority of NK cells, and approximately 24% of peripheral T-cells (65).
It is composed of a disulfide-linked homodimer of 40 kDa subunits, and has been shown to be expressed on both αβ and γδ T-cells (66).
CD161 T-cell expression has consistently been associated with a memory phenotype in adult circulations not only in αβ T-cell populations (67-70) but also in the γδ T-cell population (66).

title: Activation of human γδ T cells and NK cells by Staphylococcal enterotoxins requires both monocytes and conventional T cells
summary: Functional study of human γδ T cell subsets that co-analyses TRDV2 and CD161. TRDV2+ (Vδ2) cells are the most prevalent circulating γδ subset and produce IFN-γ on activation. CD161 is examined here as a surface/protein memory-associated marker (measured by flow cytometry) on TRDV2+ γδ T cells alongside CD27/CD28, situating CD161 as a memory/pro-inflammatory marker on the Vδ2 subset. TRDV2 is a transcript-level marker; CD161 is protein/flow here.
quotes: γδ T cells are commonly subdivided according to Vδ-chain usage, which also correlates with tissue distribution and function where TRDV2 + cells are more frequently found in circulation and TRDV1/3 + at mucosal sites.
In the circulation, the TRDV2 + subpopulation is the most prevalent among γδ T cells.

We therefore investigated whether SEinduced responses in TRDV2 + T cells associated with a particular phenotype. We specifically investigated the memory-associated markers CD27, CD28, and CD161, commonly associated with pro-inflammatory responses in memory T cells.

title: Lectin-like transcript 1 is a marker of germinal center-derived B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphomas dampening natural killer cell functions
summary: Directly localises CD161+ T cells (including small numbers of TCRγδ+ cells and TCRVα7.2+ MAIT cells) within human tonsil by immunohistochemistry and multicolor flow cytometry. CD161+ cells were found predominantly in the interfollicular zone (IFZ) surrounding germinal centers. CD161 is measured here at the PROTEIN level (anti-CD161 mAbs, flow); the snippet explicitly distinguishes CD161+ TCRγδ+ T cells from CD161-high TCRVα7.2+ MAIT cells in tonsil — direct evidence anchoring both the tonsil localisation and the γδ-vs-MAIT distinction. NOTE: 'C' in this snippet is an OCR rendering of superscript '+'.
quotes: CD161 was expressed by the majority of NK cells and by a significant proportion of T cells which were mostly composed of TCRab C T cells but also of small numbers of TCRgd C T cells and TCRVa7.2 C mucosal-associated invariant T cells characterized by the expression of high level of CD161 (Fig. 2D).
CD161 C cells were mostly found in the IFZ surrounding GC (Fig. 2A).

title: γδT CELLS IN THE PALATINE TONSIL
summary: The foundational study of gamma-delta T cells specifically in human palatine tonsil (the atlas tissue). Flow cytometry showed ~1.56% of tonsillar T cells express the γδ TCR; immunohistology localised them preferentially to the crypt epithelium, less in surface epithelium, and fewest in the interfollicular space. γδ TCR is a protein/surface identification here. Establishes the palatine-tonsil location and rarity of the γδ T cell population that the atlas Vδ2+ label sits within.
quotes: Flowcytometric analysis showed that 1.56% of T cells in palatine tonsils obtained from patients with recurrent tonsillitis (n=17) expressed the γδT cell receptor.

It was demonstrated that T cells in the crypt epithelium contained more γδT cell receptor bearing cells than did T cells infiltrating the tonsillar epithelium on the free surface. T cells in the interfollicular space included even fewer γδT cells.

title: Cytotoxic Vδ2+ T cell subsets expand in response to malaria in human tonsil and spleen organoids
summary: Functional characterisation of Vδ2+ (TRDV2+) γδ T cells in human tonsil (and spleen) organoids. Vδ2+ γδ T cells increased in abundance in tonsil organoids in response to malaria parasites, in contrast to Vδ1+ cells which did not expand. Establishes γδ T cell effector functions (cytotoxic killing, pro-inflammatory cytokines, B cell help, antigen presentation) in a secondary lymphoid / tonsil context. Vδ2 identity is defined by TCR usage; functions are cytotoxic/effector.
quotes: In this study, we found that Vδ2 + γδ T cells increase in abundance in tonsil and spleen organoids in response to malaria parasites, similarly to what has been observed in blood in malaria-naïve individuals.

They can play diverse roles, including production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, cytotoxic killing, antigen presentation, promotion of dendritic cell maturation, B cell help, recruitment of other immune cells, and secretion of growth factors [29].
γδ + T cells may also play a role in direct or indirect modulation of antibody production in secondary lymphoid organs [30][31][32][33][34]).

title: Impact of Aging on the Frequency, Phenotype, and Function of CD161-Expressing T Cells
authors: K. V. D. van der Geest
summary: Dissects which innate-like T cell lineages express CD161. Confirms gamma-delta T cells, iNKT cells, and MAIT cells can all express CD161 (protein/flow), and identifies MAIT cells separately by TCR-Vα7.2 staining — reinforcing that CD161 is shared across lineages and is NOT MAIT-specific. Supports the caveat that a CD161+ TRDV2+ cell is a γδ (Vδ2) cell with a shared CD161 marker, not a canonical MAIT cell.
quotes: Previous studies have reported that gamma-delta T cells, invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells, and MAIT cells may express CD161 (33,37,38).
To delineate MAIT cells, additional staining was performed for the TCR-Vα7.2 receptor (Figure 2E).

title: Human blood MAIT cell subsets defined using MR1 tetramers
summary: Definitional MAIT-cell paper underpinning the γδ/MAIT caveat. Canonical MAIT cells are identified by MR1-5-OP-RU tetramer staining and use the TRAV1-2 (Vα7.2) alpha-beta TCR; CD161 (high) is a widely used surrogate MAIT marker but is imperfect and not specific. This establishes that genuine MAIT cells are alpha-beta / TRAV1-2 / MR1-restricted, so CD161 alone (or CD161 with a γδ TCR) does not define a MAIT cell.
quotes: MAIT cells exhibit a unique cell surface phenotype, including expression of high levels of the C-type lectin CD161, 3 the IL-18Ra chain CD218 4 as well as the ectopeptidase CD26.

Taken together, while the CD161 HI TRAV1-2 + phenotype is a reasonably accurate indicator of CD8aa + and DN MAIT cells, for other MAIT cell populations (CD4 + , DP and CD8ab + ) this approach is not very reliable.

title: Diverse MR1-restricted T cells in mice and humans
summary: Shows MR1-restricted, MAIT-like cells can occur outside the canonical TRAV1-2+ compartment and share high CD161/CD26 with MAIT cells, but formal MAIT identity is defined by MR1 restriction and the TRAV1-2 alpha-beta TCR. Provides the conceptual frame of 'MAIT-like' innate cells that share CD161 but differ in lineage — directly relevant to labelling a TRDV2+ γδ cell as 'MAIT-like' rather than MAIT.
quotes: As expected, the majority of TRAV1-2 + MAIT cells were CD218a high and CD161 high , in contrast to MR1-5-OP-RU tetramer − 'conventional' αβ T cells, which were mostly low for these markers (Fig. 6a, second panels).

For TRAV1-2 − MR1-5-OP-RU tetramer + cells, two distinct populations emerged: some had high CD218a and CD161 expression, akin to MAIT cells (MAIT-like cells), and some had low expression of these markers (non-MAIT-like cells) (Fig. 6a, third panels).
